headline: New Zealand Q3 inflation slows to 3.7%, remaining above central bank target
summary: New Zealand's annual inflation slowed to 3.7% in the third quarter, coming in below analysts' forecasts but remaining above the top end of the central bank's target range.
why: Consumer price inflation is a primary metric central banks use to set interest rates. Readings above targets often pressure policymakers to maintain or raise rates, affecting borrowing costs and currency valuations.

impacts.name: New Zealand Banking
impacts.why: Persistent inflation keeps pressure on the central bank regarding interest rate decisions.

why_moved: Inflation readings above the central bank's target range keep rate hike expectations alive, influencing domestic bond yields and currency exchange rates.
